author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Reader metadata interfaces manually mirror the generated manifest shape with renamed fields.
findings.consequence: Any future manifest field rename or semantic change must be updated in the generated OpenAPI types, the runtime mapper, and this parallel camelCase metadata model, increasing drift risk before the final Reader page DTO is built.
findings.evidence: The owned ReaderWorkMetadataBase repeats manifest concepts such as alternateMedia, contributors, declaredPageCount, displayTitle, editorWorkId, pageStep, startPageName, titlePath, urn, and workId while shared/types/work-manifest.ts exposes ReaderManifestResponse directly from the generated API types and readerCommonMetadata maps the same backend fields into this local model.
findings.recommendation: Keep the generated ReaderManifestResponse as the metadata boundary and add only the server-only additions, such as base and normalized preferredSize, or derive this type from ReaderManifestResponse with Pick/Omit so field ownership stays tied to the generated API contract.

Inspected direct consumer server/api/reader/[author]/[title]/[page]/[mediatype].get.ts, which immediately converts this metadata into the public ReaderPage DTO.

findings.summary: Exported page type aliases duplicate generated manifest page aliases and are unused in the repository.
findings.consequence: The extra exported names add another page identity vocabulary without enforcing a policy, so future code can choose between equivalent ReaderSourcePage, ReaderFacsimileSourcePage, WorkManifestPage, and WorkManifestFacsimilePage names for the same backend concept.
findings.evidence: The owned aliases on lines 158-159 are direct aliases to WorkManifestPage and WorkManifestFacsimilePage, and repository search found no current references outside their definitions; shared/types/work-manifest.ts already exports the generated page types.
findings.recommendation: Delete the unused aliases, or move any genuinely Reader-specific page type into shared/types/reader.ts only if it adds a distinct Reader-facing contract.
